findings.claim: Lesson teaches Shakespeare's Sonnet 116 and Byron's 'She Walks in Beauty' as anthology poems: "In the OCR anthology, Romantic-era poems on love explore grand declarations of devotion..."
findings.truth: Neither poem is in the OCR Love and Relationships cluster. The 15 cluster poems are: A Broken Appointment, A Song, An Arundel Tomb, Bright Star, Dusting the Phone, Fin de Fete, I Wouldn't Thank You for a Valentine, In Paris With You, Long Distance II, Love After Love, Love and Friendship, Morning Song, Now, The Sorrow of True Love, Warming Her Pearls. 0 of 2 poems on cluster. Recommend a rebuild on real cluster poems (Bright Star, Now, A Song and Love and Friendship cover the same ground).

findings.claim: "The OCR poetry comparison (Component 02, Section A) is worth 40 marks and requires you to compare a named poem with one you choose from the collection... you must discuss both poems in a sustained, integrated comparison."
findings.truth: The compulsory poetry question has two parts. Part (a) compares a NAMED anthology poem, printed in the paper, with an UNSEEN poem, for 20 marks. Part (b) is a separate related question on a DIFFERENT anthology poem of the learner's own choice, for 20 marks. The two anthology poems are never compared with each other. A student taught this premise writes the wrong essay.

findings.claim: Tooltip on 'volta': "When form or content contradicts or undermines what has just been stated, creating irony or emotional complexity."
findings.truth: That is not what volta means; it describes bathos or undercutting. A volta is the turn where a poem's argument, tone or perspective shifts. The unit's own glossary already carries the correct definition, so the tooltip contradicted it.
findings.evidence: Unit glossary_terms entry 'volta'; standard prosody definition

findings.claim: "The rhyme scheme is deliberately comic - 'bamboozled' and 'maroonded' are almost nonsense rhymes", repeated in flashcard 9 and in practice question 4's mark scheme.
findings.truth: 'bamboozled' and 'maroonded' do not rhyme with each other and sit in different slots in the stanza. The comic invented rhyme is 'wounded' / 'maroonded': "I'm one of your talking wounded. / I'm a hostage. I'm maroonded." A student quoting the pair as printed makes a false textual claim.
findings.evidence: data/canonical_poems/ocr-love-and-relationships/in-paris-with-you.txt, lines 3-4 and line 6

findings.claim: "Harrison uses the sonnet form", with a tooltip and glossary entry defining a sonnet as "A fourteen-line poem"; a flashcard answers "A sonnet".
findings.truth: 'Long Distance II' is sixteen lines in four quatrains - a Meredithian sonnet, the sixteen-line form Harrison uses throughout 'The School of Eloquence'. Calling it a sonnet is right, but a student who also learns 'sonnet = fourteen lines' will write that the poem has fourteen lines. Corrected to name the sixteen-line form.

summary: Unit-fatal, the same pattern as the sibling poetry-conflict unit: 7 of 8 lessons teach poems that are not in the OCR Love and Relationships cluster (Edexcel and AQA Relationships poems plus Porphyria's Lover and A Woman to Her Lover), and only 4 of the 15 cluster poems appear anywhere in the unit, all of them in lesson 3. Lesson 8's whole quotation bank is for the wrong anthology. The unit also teaches a poetry question that does not exist - one 40-mark comparison of two anthology poems marked AO1 15 / AO2 15 / AO3 10 - instead of one two-part question worth 20 marks for a comparison with an unseen poem plus 20 marks for a related own-choice question. Lesson 3 is fixed in full; the exam-structure claims in lesson 7 are patched so the lesson is safe to read before a rebuild lands.
